target_customer: Enterprises deploying customer-facing AI agents (security teams)
problem: AI agents change frequently and are hard to test; attackers can inject payloads through pages, documents and tool outputs.
business_model: B2B security SaaS / continuous AI red-teaming agent
product_category: AI agent security and red teaming

founders.name: Ahmed Aly
founders.background_notes: First data scientist at a Sequoia-backed startup; published researcher.

technical_complexity.rationale: Adaptive attack agents, controlled SaaS replicas and a benchmark (ACE); needs research-grade adversarial ML.

defensibility.rationale: Library of 10,000+ attack strategies (company claim) may compound, but well-funded rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early; 2026 press shows several well-funded AI red-teaming entrants (e.g. Gray Swan, RunSybil) but none dated at founding.

market_need_then: Company says Nyx found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 firms and reached a $1.04M annualized run rate by 2026-09-11 (self-reported).

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name; Nyx product name evokes night goddess but no source states origin.

outcome_analysis: Fabraix is a Summer 2026 company, active and months old. It reports a $1.04M run rate after three months and Fortune 500 findings, all self-reported. No verified funding round exists. Too early to call; risks are a crowded, heavily funded AI security field.
notes: EveryDev directory lists $500K pre-seed; single aggregator, unverified, not recorded. TestingCatalog gives founders Ahmed Aly and Ibrahim Abdu, matching YC. No dated competitors near founding were sourced; 2026 funding news of other red-teaming firms is not tied to founding. Outcome search found no shutdown.
